output.brief:
The rise from 0.31% to 0.41% looks like ordinary week-to-week variation. Over the previous 26 weeks the rate averaged 0.35%, and the normal band's upper edge is 0.48%. The week of 26 Oct, at 0.41%, sits inside it. Three earlier weeks were higher, and the investigations of those found no fault. The burn-rate page did not fire (burn was 0.82x against a 2x threshold). The dashboard numbers were recounted from raw logs and match, so this is not a counting artefact. Bookings and customer complaints did not change.

The "new pods error twice as often" finding is a normal warm-up effect. Every recent rollout, including a config-only redeploy, shows the same gap, caused by empty caches on new pods. It adds only 10–20 errors, against roughly 2,000 extra errors in the week. It says nothing about v4.18 being faulty.

I'm fairly confident in this, though I did not test the replica move or partner-sync traffic directly. Neither is needed for the decision.

Next steps: don't roll back, and don't mute alerting. That would remove the protection for no benefit. Note the week at ops review, apply the standard check to the following week, and escalate only if that week exceeds the band or the burn-rate page fires.
